definition: A wheeled cart used to carry groceries; also an online store's virtual basket.
examples: Grab a shopping cart before we go in.
I left the milk in the shopping cart.
Your items are still in your online shopping cart.
tip: In American English, say cart rather than trolley.

definition: The visible result produced by code or software, rather than the source code.
examples: I want to see the visual output, not the code.
The visual output looks different on my phone.
Can you preview the visual output?

definition: A control that switches a setting between two states; as a verb, to switch between them.
structure: toggle something on/off; a toggle switch
examples: Add a dark-mode toggle.
Toggle the setting off and on again.
The toggle is at the top of the page.

definition: In Git, to save a snapshot of changes in a local repository; commit is both a noun and a verb.
examples: Commit the changes before you leave.
I made a commit with the new cards.
A commit doesn't automatically push the changes.
tip: Commit saves the snapshot; push sends it to the remote.

definition: In Git, to upload local commits to a remote repository.
catalan: pujar els canvis al repositori remot
structure: push commits to GitHub; push to main
examples: Push the changes to GitHub.
I haven't pushed that commit yet.
Push to the main branch after reviewing.
tip: Push sends commits away from your computer.

definition: A menu that opens to show a list of choices when selected.
structure: open / select from a drop-down menu
examples: Open the drop-down menu.
Choose your class from the drop-down.
The menu doesn't open on mobile.
tip: The options drop down from the control.

definition: A plan showing the main steps and goals for a project.
examples: We need a roadmap for the app.
The roadmap shows our next features.
Let's update the project roadmap.
tip: A roadmap shows where your project is heading.
